rows.basis: The Q2 release names AI only as one of several markets (enterprise, cloud, AI, 5G/Telco), and the MD&A credits enterprise and datacenter customers. No AI amount or share is stated. Server and storage systems ($4.46bn) is a product line, not an AI line.
The CEO calls record revenue a validation of AI accelerated compute leadership, and the MD&A ties growth to GPU, HPC and rack-scale demand from datacenter customers. No AI amount or share is stated.

The MD&A says the increased use of AI 'has substantially increased demand for our products', and the release credits AI infrastructure demand for revenue up 110% to $14.9bn. That $14.9bn is total revenue, not the AI part. No AI share is stated.

The MD&A attributes growth to GPU servers and rack-scale solutions. It says GPU & Super Racks billings rose by $5,804.0m (52%), which is an increase, not a level, so it gives no AI revenue amount. No AI share is stated in the filing.

The MD&A says Hyper Servers, GPU & Super Racks billings rose by $15,261.5m (83.4%) on GB200/GB300 systems. That is an increase, not a level. The call's 'AI solutions about 60% of fourth-quarter revenue' would support a stated_share row, but it is a quarterly figure and is not in the pack, so no amount is attributed.

The FY2026 MD&A expects 'further demand for data center expansion driven by the AI market'. Q1 FY2027 revenue is estimated at $18.5–19.5bn 'primarily due to increased demand for AI platforms', but that is a total, not an AI amount.
